newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen falling.

text.p: Gold prices are likely to fall further in the Indian sub-continent with wedding season demand yet to pick up but may firm early next year, dealers and analysts said on Monday.
"Buying for the just-commenced wedding season has been lower than expected while enough supplies kept pressure on prices," said a Bombay dealer.
The Indian wedding season starts end-November and ends in February.
Analysts said a turnaround in the second half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), coupled with funds from harvest could improve demand for bullion next month.
In the week to Monday, gold prices fell 50 rupees to 5,040 per 10 grammes.
"Arrivals of imported gold kept the market quiet," said dealer Babubhai Jain. A weak trend in the global market and a firm rupee also kept sentiment subdued during the week.
In Pakistan's commercial city of Karachi, gold prices are expected to fall further in the coming week on low demand arising from a shortage of funds, dealers said.
A liquidity crunch pushed up interbank call money rates to 20 percent, they said.
In the week to Sunday, gold lost 69 rupees to 5,156 per 10 grammes on the Karachi bullion market.
"Gold prices are expected to ease because of low demand owing to a shortage of funds," dealer Saeed Qureshi said. "People are spending less on ornaments for weddings than before."
In Dubai, the feeder market for gold demand in the Indian sub-continent, dealers said they expected the market to liven up on increased demand in the Islamic holy month of Ramadan.
Dealers said the holy month, beginning mid-January, was usually buoyant for jewellery sales as people buy gold as presents for each other.

In line with weaker international prices for bullion -- which fell to a three-year low last week -- the price of the Dubai benchmark ten tola bar fell to 5,104 dirhams ($1,390) on Sunday from 5,134 dirhams a week earlier.
"The overriding sentiment is very bearish. Prices are down and people have already stocked up inventories for Christmas. It is not a rosy picture," a leading Dubai trader said.
"But the marriage season and a good harvest should prop up demand a little," he added, in reference to the recent start in India of the marriage season after a good agricultural harvest.
Much of Dubai's demand originates in India, the world's single biggest gold market, and Pakistan.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion 1$=35.87 Indian rupees, 40.22 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams)
* Bombay prices December 9 & 2, Karachi and Dubai prices December 8 & 1 respectively.
-- Giri Venkatesan, Bombay Commodities +91-22-265 9000
